expectations.text: Identifies Clostridium perfringens as the most likely cause
expectations.evidence: Names C. perfringens type A as most likely

expectations.text: Explains that spores survive cooking and germinate/multiply rapidly during slow cooling or warm holding of the large pot
expectations.evidence: Spores survive cooking, activated; anaerobic deep pot; doubling 7-10 min overnight

expectations.text: Explains it is a toxicoinfection: large numbers eaten, enterotoxin released when cells sporulate in the gut (not a preformed toxin)
expectations.evidence: Cells sporulate in the gut releasing enterotoxin; 'not a toxin already formed in the food'

expectations.text: Uses onset time and symptoms to rule out alternatives such as S. aureus or emetic B. cereus (rapid vomiting) and Salmonella (fever)
expectations.evidence: Rules out S. aureus (2-6 h) and Salmonella/Campylobacter; notes diarrheal B. cereus as alternative

expectations.text: Gives specific cooling controls: shallow containers/portioning, ice bath or fridge so food cools quickly through the danger zone
expectations.evidence: Shallow pans <=2 in, slice roasts, ice-water bath, Food Code 2-stage cooling

expectations.text: Gives holding/reheating controls: hot hold at or above about 140 F (60 C) and reheat to about 165 F (74 C)
expectations.evidence: Reheat to 165 F / rolling boil; hot hold >=135 F (notes the book cites 140 F)
